newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end mostly up as yen falls.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end mostly up as yen falls.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures, except for silver, reversed early losses to end higher on Friday, as the dollar jumped against the yen in late Tokyo trade, Japanese traders said.

Palladium futures posted especially strong gains in afternoon trade, with the four distant months rising their 48 yen per gram daily limits before retracing by the close. Benchmark June palladium ended up 43 yen at 721 yen per gram.
"Some private investors rushed to cover short positions on the yen's sudden fall. Price movements were exaggerated by relatively thin market conditions," one commodity broker said.
Gold futures ranged from eight yen to 12 yen per gram higher. Benchmark June was up 12 yen at 1,217 yen.
Spot gold was quoted weaker at $323.40/90 per ounce at 0757 GMT, against $324.20/70 in New York on Thursday.

"Speculative interest in gold futures remains thin, with attention centring on PGMs," one trader said. He said spot gold may probe downside support at $322.00 to $323.00 amid pressure from the dollar.
In the physical market, Japan's gold demand has shown little sign of recovering, while demand for PGMs has been good, they added. --Tokyo Commodities Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
